thread:
bob_acme: Hey team — since ~09:00 UTC we're seeing a spike of 429s on POST /v1/generate. It looks minute-boundary-y: lots of requests land right at :00. We're using our custom SDK over HTTP/2 with multiplexing (~40 concurrent streams). Any quick checks?

maria_support: @bob_acme sorry about that, can you paste a raw response (headers + body) for one 429 and a sample request_id? Also roughly what RPM/TPM peaks you observed?

bob_acme: here's an example header chunk from our logs:
```
HTTP/2 429
x-request-id: req_7b2a1c
x-rate-limit-rpm: 120/120
x-rate-limit-tpm: 15000/15000
retry-after: 5
content-type: application/json
```
We see bursts to ~180 req/min (short spikes) and tokens vary — sometimes 20k TPM in a minute.

raj_infra: those headers are helpful. Tenant-level RPM cap is 120/min on your plan; TPM cap is 15k/min. The pattern you described (many streams around the top-of-minute) will push a short spike over RPM even if sustained avg < cap. We use a sliding-window bucket which still rejects when instantaneous counts exceed the per-minute budget.

maria_support: short checklist while we dig: 1) send us account_id + 09:00–09:15 UTC logs 2) include one x-request-id from a rejected call 3) confirm if you see HTTP/2 connection reuse (yes/no) 4) do you stream responses or request full payload each call?

bob_acme: will send account_id in DM. We do reuse a few long-lived connections, and we send full prompt each time.

rate-limit-bot: Alert: tenant acme-corp exceeded RPM cap (120/min) at 2026-03-17T09:00:00Z — 182 req/min observed.

zen_oncall: quick diagnostics: multiplexing over HTTP/2 can concentrate many logical requests into the same millisecond when your client opens many streams at once or the app fan-out aligns. Two immediate mitigations: add client-side spread/jitter across the minute, and cap per-connection concurrency. Also try using our streaming API for large responses — it reduces token churn per request.

devx_olivia: small reproducible test you can run locally: send 30 parallel requests within 8–12s and watch the headers. Example curl loop (attach x-client-id):
```
for i in $(seq 1 30); do
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} %{url_effective} %{stderr}" \
    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
    -H "x-client-request-id: acme-test-$i" \
    -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate &
done
wait
```
If you reproduce, capture any x-request-id from 429 responses and paste here.

bob_acme: thanks. One question: is this RPM token-bucket with refill every minute or sliding window? Our dev thinks a per-minute boundary causes refill jitter.

raj_infra: We use a sliding-window / leaky-bucket-ish implementation with short internal sub-intervals, but you can get boundary effects when client bursts align. In practice: 1) avoid minute alignment spikes, 2) implement a client token-bucket with refill granularity of 1s (not 60s), and 3) allow small bursts but keep average under limit.

maria_support: If you want immediate breathing room we can temporarily raise your RPM to 300 for 1 hour while you roll out the SDK changes; we need a confirmation from account owner. Would you like us to do that?

bob_acme: Yes please. We'll apply jitter + lower per-conn concurrency in the next 20m. Please bump for an hour.

raj_infra: Done — I've raised a temporary RPM to 300 for acme-corp for 1 hour (change id: cfg_88f). Monitor and let us know if it clears.

bob_acme: Seeing far fewer 429s now, thanks. We'll push client fix and report back.

maria_support: Followups & long-term advice: - Implement client-side token bucket pseudo-code (refill granularity 1s) and randomized jitter on release. - Prefer connection pooling with modest concurrency per connection (e.g., 6–8 streams) rather than cranking 40 streams on a single node. - Use our /v1/stream for heavy token workloads where you can stream partial responses and avoid repeated token-heavy calls. - Consider Dedicated if you expect sustained spikes; it provides reserved capacity and custom limits.

devx_olivia: example client pseudocode we recommend (simple):
```
// tokens = maxRequestsPerSec * burstFactor
tokens = capacity
onRequest() {
  if tokens > 0:
    tokens -= 1
    send()
  else:
    wait random_backoff + jitter
}
refill every 1s: tokens = min(capacity, tokens + refill_amount)
```
Tweaks: set refill_amount so rate ~ RPM/60, and burstFactor 2–3.

bob_acme: copying these notes into our runbook. Appreciate the fast triage :thumbsup: Will follow up after the client rollout.

maria_support: great — please DM the sample x-request-ids and account_id when you have them so infra can stitch traces. We're marking this thread for follow-up in case any residual 429s remain.

zen_oncall: leaving a reminder: if you still see 429s after client spread, ping us and we'll look at request-level traces and whether a routing fallback would help.

bob_acme: will do — thanks everyone!
